title: LLM-Based Test Generation: Information Sources, Generation Strategies, and Quality Evidence
datasets: No experimental benchmark or model dataset. This is a structured narrative survey based on 95 curated source records through 2026-09-29, including seven surveys/roadmaps and 88 primary-method/benchmark/empirical/historical records. SWT-Bench and TC-Bench are discussed as related benchmark examples, not evaluated.
task: Narrative synthesis organizing LLM test generation by testing objective and artifact, information access/provenance, generation/learning mechanisms, and quality evidence. Covers unit/requirements/API/GUI/fuzzing/bug reproduction and test generation for code.
input_setting: Not an empirical model input/output study. The paper proposes a conceptual framework for how test artifacts are constructed and how their quality is evidenced; it distinguishes repository tests, requirements tests, oracles, API/GUI sequences, fuzzers and bug-reproduction tests.

evaluation_route: Read the full 12,871-word / 1,032-line arXiv v1 text across all sections, references and appendices; SHA-256 e90f12464681522dca4baf78bdd9d5d90847cc75408bd27134c46d076968d26b. The paper explicitly characterizes itself as a structured narrative synthesis, not a completed systematic review: 95 curated records through 2026-09-29, seven surveys and 88 primary records; most records were abstract/metadata checked, with selected full-text passages only. It states dual independent screening, complete variant-level coding, inter-rater validation, systematic multi-database search and quantitative synthesis remain incomplete. No experimental dataset, result, model run, or reproduction is claimed. Public repository does include the 95-record CSV/Markdown register, search notes, provenance, manuscript and figure build assets; no empirical artifact to reproduce.
blockers: This is a conceptual narrative survey and makes no experiment or reproducible model-performance claim; there is no method result to rerun.

Its 95-record corpus is preliminary, not exhaustive or systematically screened: abstract/metadata inspection for most records; selected full-text passages; no independent dual screening, complete version-level extraction, inter-rater validation, or pooled analysis. Authors explicitly state this.

The public repository contains the manuscript, source register and build scripts, but no test generator/model code or experiment dataset. No repository-wide license is declared (only the bundled ACM template has its own license).
concept_fit: High background value for the thesis: clear synthesis across test objectives, behavioral information provenance, oracle quality and evaluation evidence; directly discusses SWT-Bench, TC-Bench and oracle independence. It helps distinguish issue reproduction from fault discovery, and execution success from behavioral correctness. It does not use Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT-Bench experimentally, provide a root-cause taxonomy, or test the user’s model.
recommendation: Use as a recent conceptual map and related-work discovery source, not a candidate method, model baseline, or “verified systematic review.” Its most useful organizing distinction for this thesis is between artifact generation and evidence of behavioral correctness, including independent oracle validation and the difference between known-bug reproduction and unknown-bug discovery. Cross-check each primary-paper claim against original papers. This survey’s own repository says its search and screening are preliminary and that inter-rater validation/full coding are pending. No model/code run.
